adam.headline: Takes care of the ball, defends well, and holds on contested catches.
text: Adam gives the ball away 1.4 times a game against a league middle of 2.2, and has forced 10 turnovers against 7 giveaways. His set-ups are worth 1.07 points a shot, second only to Ian's, and 39% of them go in.
On defense he is beaten on 11% of shots (middle 20%), opponents shoot 19% when he stays in front (middle 30%), and he carries 1.30x an even share of the defending. Reilly made 2 of 12 against him.

The habit to fix: when a pass reaches him with a defender close, he holds the ball first on 7 of 9 shots. His shot quality is -0.15 points a shot against the league, so a faster decision and a closer spot would help a shooter who sits right at the league middle for TS (37%).
adam.strengths: Ball security and defense: 1.4 giveaways a game and opponents at 19% when he stays in front.
workOn: Decide sooner on a contested catch: he holds the ball first on 7 of 9 of them.
Look for closer spots: his shots are worth 0.15 points a shot less than the league's.
adam.guard: Stay close when a pass reaches him. He holds the ball first on 7 of 9 contested catches, and his spots are worth less than the league's.
adam.season: Adam went 4-2 in the filmed even-team games, gave the ball away only 1.4 times a game and sits second in the Defender race.

zach.headline: Shoots the most, gets open a lot, and needs the next one to go in.
text: Zach has taken 41 shots in 6 games, 68% of them open, and made them at 31% TS against a league middle of 37%. The looks are average for where he shoots (-0.07 a shot), so this is finishing, not shot selection.

The pressure is real: 13 forced turnovers, the most in the league, against 14 giveaways. Viraj got beaten on 5 of 12 shots guarding him, but when Viraj stayed in front, Zach went 0 for 7. Opponents shoot 39% over Zach when he stays in front (middle 30%).

Rebounding is the quiet cost: 1.6 a game, and only 1.0 once uncontested ones count half, the lowest in the league. Across 54 results his teams win 13.7 points of win chance less than expected (17-37), the clearest signal in the league, and he and Adam are 2-11 as teammates.
zach.strengths: Pressure on the ball: 13 forced turnovers, the most in the league.
workOn: Grab more boards: 1.0 a game once uncontested ones count half is the lowest in the league.
Cut the giveaways: 3.1 live-ball turnovers a game against a middle of 2.2, and 27% of the trips he ends are turnovers.
zach.guard: Stay between him and the hoop. Viraj got beaten on 5 of 12 shots guarding him, but when Viraj stayed in front, Zach went 0 for 7.
zach.season: Zach took 41 shots in 6 games, forced 13 turnovers, the most in the league, and went 2-4 in the filmed even-team games.

alex.headline: Wins the boards and hands the ball back.
text: Alex is the best rebounder among players with five or more games: 3.6 a game, and 2.3 once uncontested ones count half (middle 1.9). His rebounding rating is 88, the highest of the four players rated so far.

The shots come from hard spots: 0.10 points a shot below the league, at 29% TS. When a pass reaches him in a contest he holds the ball every time (5 of 5), and the looks he sets up for others are worth 0.26 points a shot, second lowest in the league (middle 0.68).
He gives the ball away 3.2 times a game, second only to Reilly, and 23% of the trips he ends are turnovers. He is beaten on a third of shots (5 of 15), but he held Ian to 0 for 10.
alex.strengths: Rebounding: 3.6 a game and an 88 rebounding rating, the highest of the players rated.
workOn: Keep the ball: 3.2 live-ball turnovers a game against a middle of 2.2 is the biggest swing available to him.
Move it on or shoot sooner on a contested catch: he held the ball first all 5 times.
alex.guard: Close out early. He held the ball first on all 5 contested catches, and his spots are worth 0.10 points a shot below the league's.
alex.season: Alex went 1-4 in the filmed even-team games but led everyone with five games in rebounding, 3.6 a game.

ben.headline: Nobody gets past him, and he leads the MVP, Best player and Defender races.
text: Ben has never been tagged as beaten, 0 of 12 shots. Opponents shoot 17% when he is in position, and Adam, one of the better scorers, is 5 of 14 against him. He leads the MVP race (23.4 over 5 games), the Defender race (10.0) and Best player (6.1 a game).

He scores at 49% TS, well above the league middle of 37%, from spots worth 0.34 points a shot more than the league's, even though only 27% of his shots are open. He gives the ball away 1.0 times a game, the fewest in the league, and his overall rating of 85 is the highest of the four players rated so far.

He sets up 4.1 shots a game worth 0.68 points a shot, about the league middle, but only 29% go in, and teammates held the ball first on 3 of his 7 contested set-ups. Over 55 results his teams win 7.8 points of win chance more than expected (33-22).
ben.strengths: Defense and ball security: never beaten, opponents at 17% in position, 1.0 giveaways a game.
workOn: Rebound more: it is his lowest rating (69), and 1.7 a game once uncontested ones count half is under the league middle of 1.9.
Make the pass easier to finish: only 29% of his set-ups go in.
ben.guard: There is no soft spot on film. Stay close: only 27% of his shots are open and he still scores at 49% TS.
ben.season: Ben led the MVP, Best player and Defender races at 6.1 two-way a game, gave the ball away 1.0 times a game and was never beaten on a shot.

g-ian.headline: Stays in front of everyone and sets up the best looks, a few at a time.
text: Ian is beaten on 9% of shots (1 of 11) and held Alex to 4 of 20, the busiest matchup on film. When opponents do shoot over him, though, they hit 40%.
His set-ups are worth 1.31 points a shot, the best in the league (middle 0.68), and half of them go in, but he makes only 1.8 a game. He and Adam are 3-1 together, the top pair in the Best duo race.

He has taken 15 shots in 4 games at 27% TS, so scoring is not his job yet. His rebounds are hard-won, 71% of them contested. He is also the most improved player, up 3.3 two-way a game from his early games to his late ones.
g-ian.strengths: Staying in front and passing: beaten on 9% of shots, and his set-ups are worth 1.31 points a shot, the best in the league.
workOn: Cut the turnovers: 9 giveaways against 6 forced, and 38% of the trips he ends are turnovers.
Keep a hand up after the stop: opponents hit 40% when they shoot over him, 4 of 10.
g-ian.guard: Make him defend a shot. He is beaten on only 9% of shots, but opponents make 40% of the ones they take over him.
g-ian.season: Ian went 3-1 in the filmed even-team games, was beaten on 9% of shots and made the biggest climb in the league, up 3.3 two-way a game.

evan.headline: Three games, three wins, and the best looks of anyone with real volume.
text: Evan scores at 58% TS on shots worth 0.43 points more than the league average, the best in the league, and only 37% of his shots are open. He gives it away 1.3 times a game and forced 11 turnovers against 4 giveaways, the best trade in the league.

He passes a lot, 6.0 set-ups a game, the most in the league, but into tough spots worth 0.48 points a shot. Most of his assists came from teammates holding and then making a contested shot, so his Real AST is 0.6 against 1.6 assists.

He carries a light defensive load (0.67x an even share) and was beaten on 2 of 6 shots. His +29 on Win chance added is the most in the league, and he is 12-4 over every result. Three filmed games is still an early read.
evan.strengths: Shot quality and the turnover trade: spots worth 0.43 points a shot more than the league's, 11 forced against 4 giveaways.
workOn: Pass to better spots: his 6.0 set-ups a game are worth 0.48 points a shot against a league middle of 0.68, and only 26% go in.
Take on more of the defending: he carries 0.67x an even share, so there is room.
evan.guard: Stay with him early. Only 37% of his shots are open and he still scores at 58% TS.
evan.season: Evan won all 3 of his filmed even-team games, scored at 58% TS and had the most Win chance added in the league (+29).

g-lukas.headline: Seven shots, good looks, and the most rebounds in the league.
text: Lukas has 71% TS on shot quality of +0.32, above the league middle, but on 7 shots in 3 games.

He plays off the ball, with almost no set-ups (0.4 a game), and is rarely the tagged defender (0.39x an even share). When he is, the shots have gone in (beaten on 2 of 5), on far too few to judge. He rebounds more than anyone, 3.9 a game, 2.8 once uncontested ones count half.
His teams are 11-3 over every result, +9.2 points of win chance from having him. Three filmed games is still an early read.
g-lukas.strengths: Rebounding: 3.9 a game, the most in the league.
workOn: Take a few more shots: 7 shots in 3 games at 71% TS is too few to say what he can do.
Cut the turnovers: 2.6 live-ball turnovers a game against a middle of 2.2, and 46% of the 13 trips he ended were turnovers.
g-lukas.guard: Not enough shots to find a pattern. Box him out: he rebounds more than anyone.
g-lukas.season: Lukas went 2-1 in the filmed even-team games, led everyone in rebounding at 3.9 a game, and his teams are 11-3 over every result.

reilly.headline: Draws the heaviest assignments and leads the league in assists.
text: Reilly carries the heaviest defensive load in the league, 1.40x an even share. He is rarely beaten (13%), but opponents still hit 43% over him, which is what guarding the best scorers looks like. Adam is 1 of 8 against him when he stays in front.

He leads the league with 2.3 assists a game, and his set-ups are worth 1.01 points a shot with 55% going in. His own shots come from the lowest-value spots in the league (-0.30 a shot), even though 73% of them are open.

The ball is the problem: 3.4 live-ball turnovers a game, the most in the league, and only 3 forced against 9 giveaways. Over 23 results his teams win 5.4 points of win chance more than expected (13-10). Three filmed games is still an early read.
reilly.strengths: Passing and the toughest defensive jobs: 2.3 assists a game and 1.40x an even share of the defending.
workOn: Keep the ball: 3.4 live-ball turnovers a game against a middle of 2.2, and 38% of the trips he ends are turnovers.
Find better spots: 73% of his shots are open, but the spots are worth 0.30 points a shot less than the league's.
reilly.guard: Sag off the shot, because his spots are the lowest-value in the league, and watch the pass: his 2.3 assists a game are the most.
reilly.season: Reilly went 1-2 in the filmed even-team games, led the league with 2.3 assists a game and took the heaviest defensive load, 1.40x an even share.

viraj.headline: Gets beaten half the time, and wins the possession when he doesn't.
text: Viraj has been beaten on 8 of 16 shots, the highest rate in the league. When he stays in front, opponents shoot 25%, and Zach went 0 for 7 against him.
On offense he has 8 shots in 3 games at 25% TS, and his set-ups go to low-value spots (0.17 points a shot, the lowest in the league).
He is 0-3 on film with -28 on Win chance added, but 6-6 over every result, and his win impact is too close to call. Three filmed games is still an early read.
viraj.strengths: Contesting when in position: opponents shoot 25% against him when he stays in front.
workOn: Staying in front is the whole game: he is beaten on 8 of 16, yet opponents shoot 25% when he holds position.
Take care of the ball: 47% of the 15 trips he ended were turnovers.
viraj.guard: Not enough shots to find a pattern: 8 in 3 games at 25% TS. Let him shoot.
viraj.season: Viraj went 0-3 in the filmed even-team games, but when he stayed in front opponents shot 25% against him.
